citation: Artstein, R.; Poesio, M. Survey Article: Inter-Coder Agreement for Computational Linguistics. Computational Linguistics 34(4):555-596.
research_question: Which agreement measures match which annotation tasks?
method: Methodological survey of agreement measures and their assumptions.
finding: Agreement must be interpreted against the annotation task and units rather than reported as a context-free scalar.
applicability_to_ARPipe: Directly supports a task-specific agreement matrix; not evidence about Indian annual-report boundaries.
limitation: Survey rather than an annual-report annotation study.

citation: Hayes, A. F.; Krippendorff, K. Answering the Call for a Standard Reliability Measure for Coding Data. Communication Methods and Measures 1(1):77-89.
research_question: How should independent-coder reliability be designed and reported?
method: Conceptual and methodological comparison of reliability coefficients.
finding: Reliability evidence requires independently generated records for appropriate units; Krippendorff alpha accommodates different scales, coder counts, and missing data.
applicability_to_ARPipe: Supports blind independent annotation and alpha only where the measurement model is appropriate.
limitation: Does not prescribe ARPipe's spans, sample size, or acceptance threshold.

citation: Zapf, A.; Castell, S.; Morawietz, L.; Karch, A. Measuring inter-rater reliability for nominal data - which coefficients and confidence intervals are appropriate? BMC Medical Research Methodology 16:93.
research_question: How should uncertainty for categorical agreement be reported?
method: Simulation comparison of Fleiss K and Krippendorff alpha with asymptotic and bootstrap intervals.
finding: Bootstrap intervals performed better than the studied asymptotic interval; alpha is preferable where ratings are missing or have higher than nominal order.
applicability_to_ARPipe: Supports reporting point estimates with bootstrap intervals and avoiding unexplained universal cut-offs.
limitation: Simulation is not an annual-report study and does not validate a specific bootstrap cluster design for ARPipe.

citation: Fournier, C. Evaluating Text Segmentation using Boundary Edit Distance. ACL 2013.
research_question: How should ordered boundaries and segmentation agreement be assessed?
method: Introduces boundary similarity and related inter-coder agreement adaptations.
finding: Boundary-aware measures can give partial credit for near misses and expose properties obscured by a single exact-boundary rate.
applicability_to_ARPipe: Supports reporting exact and tolerance/distance/span measures together for MD&A boundaries.
limitation: Topic segmentation differs from physical page-span localization.

citation: Pevzner, L.; Hearst, M. A. A Critique and Improvement of an Evaluation Metric for Text Segmentation. Computational Linguistics 28(1):19-36.
research_question: What are the limitations of window-based segmentation metrics?
method: Analysis of Pk and proposal of WindowDiff.
finding: Window-based metrics have non-obvious error weighting and should not replace direct, interpretable boundary reporting without justification.
applicability_to_ARPipe: Supports retaining exact start/end, distances, and span IoU rather than using a single window metric for ARPipe.
limitation: Not an annual-report annotation study; does not establish the final ARPipe evaluator.

citation: Fort, K.; Sagot, B. Influence of Pre-Annotation on POS-Tagged Corpus Development. Fourth Linguistic Annotation Workshop.
method: Controlled experiments comparing manual annotation and pre-annotation.
finding: Pre-annotation may improve speed but creates bias that must be considered.
applicability_to_ARPipe: Supports prohibiting ARPipe predictions, OCR output, and prior annotations during independent Gold work.
limitation: POS tagging is not page transcription or MD&A localization.

citation: Anderson, M. et al. Anchoring and Agreement in Syntactic Annotations.
method: Controlled comparison of parser-assisted and human-only annotation.
finding: Editing pre-existing annotations produced anchoring effects and could overestimate system performance.
limitation: Preprint and syntactic domain; used as corroborative rather than sole evidence.

citation: Securities and Exchange Board of India. Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, last amended July 25 2022.
research_question: What is the regulatory role and historical period of an MD&A report?
finding: Regulation 34(2)(e) places a management discussion and analysis report in the annual report as part of or additional to the directors report; the 2015 regulations take effect ninety days after Gazette publication and rescind prior listing-agreement circulars subject to savings.
applicability_to_ARPipe: Provides post-2015 listed-entity context only; it cannot determine a physical boundary in a particular report.
limitation: A 2022 consolidation must not be applied as a content or boundary definition to pre-LODR corpus records without period-specific verification.

citation: Label Studio. Ways to do document annotation in Label Studio.
research_question: Can Label Studio support long document image annotation and coordinate export?
finding: Community workflows use externally hosted page images and item_index; native PDF capability and stated page limits vary by edition.
applicability_to_ARPipe: Supports the documented Community image-workflow constraints; complemented by the local synthetic POC.
limitation: Vendor documentation is not an independent long-report or blinding evaluation.

research_question: Can Prodigy preserve multi-annotator records and support review?
finding: Review groups records from multiple annotators and retains annotator/session metadata; interface-specific and deployment-specific safeguards still require validation.
applicability_to_ARPipe: Shows a plausible configurable alternative for review/provenance, not demonstrated for 100-600 page ARPipe reports.
limitation: No local POC and no license/runtime validation in this worktree.

research_question: Is doccano suitable for page-image, coordinate, and long-report annotation?
method: Official project description and installation documentation.
finding: The stated core scope is collaborative text classification, sequence labeling, and sequence-to-sequence annotation.
applicability_to_ARPipe: Supports treating doccano as text-centric and requiring customization/evidence before it is proposed for ARPipe page images.
limitation: README does not prove absence of an extension or custom workflow.

citation: ARPipe custom local interface feasibility POC, artifacts/t0_4_gold_method_research/poc/results_custom.json.
research_question: Can a local prototype serve synthetic 2-, 20-, and 600-page documents with isolation and provenance?
method: Automated local browser/API harness using synthetic PDFs only.
finding: Lazy page rendering, 600-page navigation, coordinate round-trip, append-only per-annotator records, and role-gated comparison were demonstrated; authentication was intentionally absent.
applicability_to_ARPipe: Directly relevant feasibility evidence but not a production-security or usability study.
limitation: Synthetic inputs, one machine, unauthenticated roles, and no human usability study.

citation: ARPipe Label Studio Community feasibility POC, artifacts/t0_4_gold_method_research/poc/results_label_studio.json and results_label_studio_nav.json.
research_question: Can Label Studio Community manage synthetic long-document image annotation?
method: Automated local browser/API harness using synthetic 2-, 20-, and 600-page documents.
finding: The 600-page image-list task opened and navigated; coordinate export round-tripped, but Community annotations were visible across users and required provenance was absent from export.
applicability_to_ARPipe: Directly relevant edition-specific evidence; identifies customization and isolation requirements.
limitation: Synthetic inputs, one local version, no production load/security test, and not proof for all Label Studio editions.
